title: Coordinate dependence of a Fourier component
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. For every integer $n\geq 0$, every function $f\colon \Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and every set of coordinates $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the sum of the Fourier terms indexed by multi-indices whose support is exactly $J$ depends only on the coordinates in $J$: whenever $x,y\in\Omega^n$ agree on all coordinates in $J$, this sum has the same value at $x$ and $y$.
hypotheses_covered: finite Fourier basis $B$ with its specified constant-one vector and orthonormality
points $x,y$ agreeing on every coordinate in $J$
